notes: Review only official-nine-qa-retest-2026-10-11/run-1. Do not overwrite past gold or outputs. Keyword matches, valid numeric claims, and a table proof do not excuse contradictory published refusals or missing model assignments.

source_inspection.scope: All nine preserved published answers from one fresh, one-attempt-per-question host-code run. Visually inspected 11 complete Poppler pages, including material headings, table metric/task columns, references, author grid/footnotes and architecture provenance. Transformer page 1 had Poppler missing-font warnings but the author names/order and dagger footnote were legible and checked. Not independent expert peer review, frontend end-to-end acceptance, fresh parsing, all PDFs or six-module acceptance.

sixth-author.reason: Transformer physical page 1 author grid gives Aidan N. Gomez sixth in layout order, University of Toronto and the reported email. The dagger footnote says work performed while at Google Brain; the answer distinguishes affiliation from work location rather than replacing the affiliation.

adam-settings.reason: Transformer physical page 7 Optimizer paragraph explicitly assigns beta1=0.9 and beta2=0.98, matching the published pair and cited passages.

base-gpus.reason: Transformer physical page 7 Hardware and Schedule says one machine with eight NVIDIA P100 GPUs and covers the base model, matching both claims.

bleu-improvement.reason: The table proof correctly selects EN-DE BLEU 28.4 versus previous best including ensembles 26.36 and derives 2.04. However, the third model claim, citing the same table among its anchors, asserts the exact previous-best value is unavailable and an exact difference cannot be calculated. The published answer is internally contradictory; reject despite all keyword facts matching and runtime flagging complete. No older/newer French score or FLOPs column may replace the EN-DE gold.

layernorm-reference.reason: Transformer physical page 10 References [1] gives Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, Geoffrey E Hinton, Layer normalization and 2016; the answer matches the full names/year without invented metadata.

bert-inheritance.reason: Transformer physical page 2 specifies encoder sublayers, residual/LN and the decoder including encoder-decoder attention. BERT physical page 3 says multilayer bidirectional Transformer encoder, implementation almost identical to the original, and bidirectional rather than GPT's left-constrained attention. The answer separately dual-cites inheritance and decoder-removal conclusions, explicitly labelling both as architecture inferences and not asserting BERT keeps the original six-layer or 512-dimensional configuration.

gpt-parameter-evolution.reason: The table and equivalence sources on GPT-2 physical page 4 support the qualified original-GPT 117M baseline inference and GPT-2 1542M main variant. GPT-3 physical page 8 supports eight sizes and 175B, and page 31 supports its roughly two-orders-of-magnitude data/model comparison. All main factual claims are supported; however, the live runtime fails to recognize the labelled baseline assignment and marks GPT-1 incomplete. Retain the failure, rather than reinterpreting a later local grammar fix as fresh acceptance.

gpt2-ln-change.reason: GPT-2 physical page 4 explicitly moves LN to each sub-block input and adds a final LN after the final self-attention block. The answer cites this and does not invent an explicit GPT-1 paper post-norm statement.

context-evolution.reason: GPT-2 physical page 4 and GPT-3 physical page 43 correctly support the reported 1024 and 2048 windows. GPT-1 physical page 5 only reports a 512-token training sequence. The refusal is cautious about that training sentence, but fails to use the already supplied GPT-2 architectural configuration comparison for a clearly qualified GPT-1 512-token inference. The published answer is incomplete; mentioning 512 in the refusal or GPT-2 comparison does not answer GPT-1.
